lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: recognizing linear, quadratic, and exponential situations
lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: recognizing linear, quadratic, and exponential situations

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: These two examples show the same idea in two different formats.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A population of 600 grows by 3% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 7 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 46 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 2, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: A stays ahead permanently because 46 is larger than 2.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 500(0.88)^t, with t in years. What does 0.88 represent?
choices: the fraction of value retained each year, 0.88, meaning a 12% annual loss
the number of years until the asset is worthless
the value of the asset when it was new, $500
the total value lost over the asset's life

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (5, 8) and (9, 16). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A table of successive outputs reads 8, 11, 14, 17. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 3.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 3.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.

items.prompt: A population of 1100 grows by 10% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 7 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 103 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: The two grow at the same eventual rate.
A stays ahead permanently because 103 is larger than 3.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 2500(0.97)^t, with t in years. What does 0.97 represent?
choices: the fraction of value retained each year, 0.97, meaning a 3% annual loss
the value of the asset when it was new, $2500
the number of years until the asset is worthless
the total value lost over the asset's life

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (3, -13) and (6, -37). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
